libmus_song.note: libmus song file, loaded whole by func_80052914 from a T6/T6_alias pair and started by func_80129EE0/func_80129F10 -> func_8012C4B0. The 0x38-byte header holds the fixed 0x215 signature, channel_count (+4) and instrument_count (+8, the length of the u16 table; every entry is read). Seven file offsets at +0x0C..+0x24 are relocated by func_8012C300: channel/volume/pitch tables, envelopes, keymaps, instruments and the master stream. +0x28 is the relocation flag (0 in ROM) and +0x2C..+0x37 are a zero reserve; the parser requires all four words to be zero. Master and channel streams are decoded with func_8012AF30 (note, velocity while readVelocity, var-len ticks unless the 0x8B default is active) and the 45 D_801487D0 handlers 0x80..0xAC. Their operand lengths are in the parser, read off the matched handlers. Each stream is then executed with func_801296E4/func_80129750 loop semantics, and every executed byte must have the role the linear decode gave it. At most four loops may be active (the four func_801296E4 saved-state slots). A mapped note stores keyMap[note].instrument into +0xAE, which persists across 0x9F, and table reads are collected in execution order (song voices read instruments[+0xAE] for every unmapped event, rests included). Keymap (6 B) and envelope (7 B) regions are whole records, and every record is referenced. Volume/pitch streams follow the func_8012BA20/func_8012BADC grammar (value, or value|0x80 + 1-2 byte wait). Their extent is the consumer's exact level read schedule, restated in integers from the matched code, for the default model state (rate 60, scale 0x80): func_8012C004 resets every voice (time 0, waits 1, step 0x6000/D_801CA6E4 with D_801CA6E4 = 60 from func_80129C2C for NTSC/MPAL, +0x98 = 0x80; func_8012A654, the song-volume call, can later rescale +0x98/+0x9C and is outside this model); func_8012C690 unpauses the song in one frame (queued by func_8012A870, drained by func_8012AB24/func_8012ABAC); func_8012ACC0 runs voices in slot order, adds step9C to time0C, calls func_8012AF30 while next3C - time0C < 0 (next3C += ticks << 8 per note), skips a voice whose cursor 0x80 cleared, then calls func_8012BA20/func_8012BADC while due14/due18 < time0C, which advance them by 0x100 per level tick; 0x85 (func_80129384) sets step9C = (T*0x6000/120)/60*+0x98>>7 for every voice of the song; func_801296E4/func_80129750 save and restore level cursors and waits but not due14/due18. The master takes slot 0..3 (func_8012C138) and so runs before every channel; a master stolen into a later slot is covered by also evaluating next-frame tempo delivery. Both starts the game uses are evaluated: func_80129EE0 (every voice at time 0) and func_80129F10 (func_80052944 starts T6 records 9/49/57 with marker 0 and 36/38 through func_80052AD8 with a runtime marker; func_80051D94 starts T6_alias records 2/3 that way), in which every populated voice (the master and each channel with a note stream, level streams or not) first seeks, in slot order, before the unpause is queued: commands run through their handlers; notes read velocity and duration with func_80129F10's own rule (an explicit duration clears readTicks +0xB7 even when defaultTicks is 0, where func_8012AF30 keeps it; the keymap note start that stores +0xAE is not run) and add to time0C, until the first 0xAB whose id is the marker (clock M, duration d, not executed); then next3C = M, +0x9A = d, time0C = (M - d) << 8 and one unconditional func_8012BA20/func_8012BADC call, a do-while that runs at least one tick, reads level positions 1..max(1, M - d); loops pushed during the seek saved the untouched level cursor. A selected d of 0x7FFF makes func_8012ACC0 skip func_8012AF30 for good while time and level updates continue, so that start is refused, as a 0x7FFF note duration in playback is (an unselected 0xAB with 0x7FFF is only skipped operands). Every voice of every start is run to 0x80 or to the repetition of its endless-loop state with every executed byte's role checked against the linear decode, so a start that would decode bytes differently is refused; playback instrument indices must lie inside the table; a channel 0x85 is refused. The parser does not know which start a record selects, so it requires all of them: func_80129EE0 and func_80129F10 with every marker id the song holds, each in both master orders; a seek that can never return makes the start impossible and refuses the song. Each voice's level positions are followed segment by segment (restores start new segments) until the endless loop's phase on the frame grid repeats. In every start every event of every level region must be read; a voice reading past its region's last event continues into the next region in address order, which is accepted only while that region is another level region (events of both meet on the boundary). A read of a non-level byte, a marker start whose seek never returns or that leaves a level-bearing voice silent, a tempo change inside the master's endless loop or a tempo command in a channel refuses the song. The schedule was checked against an independent frame emulator written from the matched func_80129EE0/func_80129F10/func_8012ACC0/func_8012AF30/func_8012BA20/func_8012BADC code (its own seek duration rule, +0x9A stop gate, seek of every populated voice and marker discovery): 212 start/order runs (164 func_80129EE0, 48 func_80129F10) over the 82 T6 songs it can schedule, 30,000 frames each, gave identical volume and pitch bytes per channel (the 4 songs with tempo changes inside the master's endless loop are refused and were not compared); this is finite-horizon corroboration, not a proof of every steady-state phase. Fill: zeros to word alignment after an odd instrument table, zeros to 16 at the end. Optional layer B: a song whose only refusal is a level read running from its last level region into the master stream may be closed when its witness declares that over-read exactly as params.dual_read: for each voice the channel, the level stream (volume/pitch), its own level region, the boundary (the master offset, header +0x24), level_ticks (the level ticks its region chain holds before that boundary), voice_span_ticks (note ticks until the voice first restores its endless loop under func_80129EE0), reads (every start/order in which the over-read happens, with the voice's furthest level position there; starts in which it does not happen are absent), cause, and every over-read event (song offset, bytes, value, wait, read step), which must be the same in every start that over-reads. The parser recomputes the over-read from the schedule in every start and requires the declaration to be identical; every over-read byte lies inside the master stream's decoded extent and keeps only its master-stream span, and region boundaries come from the header and tables alone. Causes, recomputed too: loop_restores_after_level_data (45 songs) when the voice's endless loop restores only after the level data runs out (voice_span_ticks > level_ticks), so func_8012BA20/func_8012BADC consume the first master bytes before func_80129750 rewinds the level cursor; restore_keeps_level_clock (10 songs) when the spans are equal but func_80129750 restores the level cursor and wait and not due14/due18, so under func_80129EE0 a later pass runs on by less than one frame step; seek_update_runs_one_tick (2 songs, 0xdf04c0 and 0xdf0770, marker-0 starts only) when the spans are equal and the unconditional do-while func_8012BA20/func_8012BADC call of func_80129F10 gives the voice a one-tick head start that the restores carry to a later pass. The over-read is the master's first 3 bytes in 52 songs: 85 FF 60 (its tempo-255 command) read as value 5 with a wait of (0x7F << 8) + 0x60 + 2 = 32,610 ticks in 38, 95 FF 85 (its endless loop start) with 32,647 ticks in 12, and 85 F0 60 / 85 C8 60 once each; 5 songs read 4 or 5 events (up to 9 bytes); in every case the last wait outlasts the voice's remaining reach, so nothing further is read.

libmus_fxbank.note: libmus fx bank installed by func_8012A910. Header: count +0, effect_count +4, instrument_count +8, flags +0xC = 0, ptr_bank +0x10 = 0 (both required zero), u16 instrument-table offset +0x14. It is followed by count {stream offset, priority} entries, which func_8012A910, func_8012C330 and func_8012C3E0 read at bank+8i+0x18/+0x1C. Streams decode and execute as fx voices (readVelocity clear, owner +0x74 null, so 0x90/0x9E are rejected; at most four active loops). The 0xA7 sub-effect calls (func_80129A44 -> func_8012C3E0) are exactly entries effect_count..count-1, and instrument references are exactly 0..instrument_count-1. A 1-byte remainder before an even instrument table is framework pad, so it must be zero. Zeros to 16 at the end.

Every other opcode below 0x80 fetches nothing. Codes 0x80 and above are text: func_801EE7B8_1406D8 fetches a trail byte (entry 0x1406F0, base 1) after a 0xFx lead. 0x1D calls func_801EF7F0_141710(slot 0); only its function 0x5E (jtbl 0x14819C -> jal func_801EB208_13D128 at 0x142890) fetches: up to 20 code slots ended by 0x11, a 0xFx lead and trail taking two, each code its own instance (loop fetch 0x13D1A8 base 0, trail fetch 0x13D1F0 base 1).
